name: Coral bleaching
summary: No fifth global bleaching event declared by NOAA as of 17 Nov; El Niño heat raises the risk of one
state: NOAA Coral Reef Watch's status page, last updated 2 Jun, says the fourth global bleaching event likely ended in 2025, and no fifth event has been declared since (NOAA). A Global Coral Reef Monitoring Network report released on 31 Aug said another event this year was very likely given El Niño conditions (bdnews24). Searches on 17 Nov found no new global declaration or confirmed regional mass bleaching, so Normal holds with an upward trend.
for_you: Bleaching mainly affects reef ecosystems and the fisheries and tourism that depend on them. NOAA Coral Reef Watch publishes current heat-stress alerts for reef areas.
rubric_hit: No global bleaching event declared by NOAA = Normal

sources.title: NOAA Coral Reef Watch — Current global bleaching status
bdnews24 — Coral bleaching occurring too frequently for reefs to recover

why: Reefs support a quarter of marine species and coastal economies; mass bleaching is a direct sign of ocean heat stress.
drivers: Marine heatwaves, El Niño, warming trend.

rubric.alert: Bleaching extent at record levels with active new alerts in the past month.
rubric.watch: Global bleaching event in progress, or regional mass bleaching.
rubric.normal: No global bleaching event in progress.
